texts.preamble: Sukhnandan Jain vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 7 March, 2025 Neutral Citation No. 2025:Mphc-Jbp:10866 1 In The High Court Of Madhya Pradesh At Jabalpur Before Hon'Ble Shri Justice Suresh Kumar Kait, Chief Justice & Hon'Ble Shri Justice Vivek Jain On The 7 th Of March, 2025 Writ Appeal No. 623 of 2025 Sukhnandan Jain Versus The State Of Madhya Pradesh And Others Appearance: Shri Mahendra Pateria with Shri Vishal Pateriya, Ad appellant. Shri Abhijeet Awasthi, Deputy Advocate respondents/State. Order
texts.facts: When the writ petition came up for hearing, Shri Abhishek Pandey, Advocate for petitioner appeared on 24.02.2025, however, the counsel who had filed the writ petition, was not available, therefore, the interim order was vacated. 4. The writ petition is pending challenging the order of the respondents whereby the authorities have directed to register an FIR.
texts.arguments: 2. The appellant filed the writ petition stating that in respect of the alleged shortage of food articles, the respondents are themselves responsible for not taking preventive measures and proper arrangements for avoiding theft of food article during transit and damage caused to the food article due to heavy rain as the food articles were lying in the open sky and there were no safety NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-JBP:10866 2 WA-623-2025 measures of keeping the food articles safely and further there were no proper arrangement for avoiding theft of food articles in the dead of night by the miscreants and reduction in the weight of the food articles due to heat of the summer season and therefore for that reason and for the other reasons mentioned in the petition, the writ petitioner cannot be made responsible for the shortage in any manner and therefore, the impugned order is absolutely arbitrary and illegal and cannot sustain in the eyes of law and is liable to be [LEAKAGE_MASK]. 3. The writ petition was filed in the year 2018 and the interim order was granted by the writ court not to register FIR, vide order dated 30.11.2018.
texts.petitioner_arguments: 2. The appellant filed the writ petition stating that in respect of the alleged shortage of food articles, the respondents are themselves responsible for not taking preventive measures and proper arrangements for avoiding theft of food article during transit and damage caused to the food article due to heavy rain as the food articles were lying in the open sky and there were no safety NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-JBP:10866 2 WA-623-2025 measures of keeping the food articles safely and further there were no proper arrangement for avoiding theft of food articles in the dead of night by the miscreants and reduction in the weight of the food articles due to heat of the summer season and therefore for that reason and for the other reasons mentioned in the petition, the writ petitioner cannot be made responsible for the shortage in any manner and therefore, the impugned order is absolutely arbitrary and illegal and cannot sustain in the eyes of law and is liable to be [LEAKAGE_MASK]. 3. The writ petition was filed in the year 2018 and the interim order was granted by the writ court not to register FIR, vide order dated 30.11.2018.
